title.value: Global signal topography in the human brain differs systematically across the lifespan
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated in the paper.
title.quote:
Global signal topography in the human brain differs systematically across the lifespan

Jason S. Nomi , Danilo Bzdok , Jingwei Li , Taylor Bolt , Salome Kornfeld ,
Zachary T. Goodman , B.T. Thomas Yeo , R. Nathan Spreng, , & Lucina Q. Uddin

extractions.description: The paper examines global signal regression in fMRI data and its impact on functional connectivity across different age groups. It highlights how global signal topography varies with age and discusses the implications for neuroscience research.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on neuroscience, particularly on the methodological aspects of functional connectivity in the brain across the lifespan. This is not directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: These findings have critical implications for lifespan network neuroscience investigations, given that a widely-used data denoising step differentially impacts brain connectivity effects in different age cohorts.

primary_category.justification: The main theme of the paper relates to neuroscience and does not align with any specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category.
primary_category.quote:
One of the biggest challenges in neuroscience is separating signal from noise (1). In
functional neuroimaging generally, and in human connectomics investigations utilizing resting
state functional MRI (fMRI) specifically, this challenge has been met with the development of
processing pipelines that mitigate artifacts known to obscure the underlying neural signal (2).

secondary_categories.justification: The research discussed does not secondarily pertain to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
secondary_categories.quote: The global signal also includes important neural activity. Animal studies show that the fMRI global blood-oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) signal is strongly associated with neuronal activity using photometry imaging of neurons (5) and intracranial electrical recordings (6).

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit into any specific sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as it primarily focuses on neuroscientific aspects of brain imaging.
primary_sub_category.quote: Global signal regression has been widely adopted as a robust method for attenuating cardiac and respiratory noise and other non-random confounding signals (2) and has also been shown to improve prediction of behavior from functional connectivity (FC) indices in certain scenarios (4).

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper's subject matter does not cover sub-categories that fall under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
secondary_sub_categories.quote:
Several lines of emerging evidence suggest a cautious approach is warranted when
exercising what is sometimes viewed as an aggressive data cleaning strategy.

applications.justification: The paper does not provide any significant application directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
applications.quote:
In a population neuroscience study of >1000 subjects,
global signal topography was related to an axis of positive and negative life outcomes and
psychological function, particularly weighted in frontoparietal executive control network
regions, in 22-37 year-old adults (8).

new_primary_category.justification: While it does not fall into an existing sustainable development category, it focuses on methodologies related to brain signal processing in neuroscience.
new_primary_category.quote:
We show distinct linear and quadratic lifespan global signal
topography associations with age. We also show that global signal regression significantly
influences age-functional connectivity strength associations.

new_primary_sub_category.value: fMRI Data Processing and Signal Regression
new_primary_sub_category.justification: The specific focus on global signal regression in the context of fMRI data processing is central to the paper.
new_primary_sub_category.quote:
Global signal regression effectively mitigates noise in fMRI data but also inadvertently removes
neural signals of interest.
